faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.whatA: BeyondPilot is an AI startup funded by GenAI Fund. It helps you discover AI solutions, find AI talent, explore enterprise use cases and projects, and connect with AI events and programs.
faq.whoA: Enterprises looking for AI solutions and builders, AI companies and startups with something to offer, and AI specialists looking for projects.
faq.findQ: How does BeyondPilot help me find relevant AI solutions or talent?
faq.findA: Search across AI solutions, talent, use cases, events, and programs from one place, then open a listing to see what it offers and how to take the next step.
faq.listQ: Can I list my solution or express interest in a project?
faq.listA: Organizations can create a profile and list their AI solutions. Use cases and projects show how to get in touch with the enterprise or with GenAI Fund. Some actions are still being built and are labelled as coming soon.
faq.applyQ: How do I apply to a challenge or program?
faq.applyA: Open the program, read its brief and eligibility, and use its Apply button. Each program lists its own dates and rules, so check its page for the details.
faq.runsQ: Who is building BeyondPilot, and how is GenAI Fund involved?
faq.runsA: BeyondPilot is an AI startup with its own product, funded by GenAI Fund, the AI-focused fund connecting enterprises with AI builders across Southeast Asia. The product is built with a development partner, shown in the team section.

useCases.title: Use cases in this challenge
useCases.lead: The business problems Tasco has published for this challenge. Open one to read its goal, requirements, budget and timeline.

challenge.title: The challenge
challenge.lead: Compulsory motor insurance is something nearly every driver in Vietnam has to carry. It is mandated and priced by regulation, so every provider offers the same cover at the same price — and when a product is regulated into sameness, the experience around it stops improving.

paper.title: It's still paper
paper.text: Lose the paper and, in every way that matters, you've lost the policy.

must.title: People buy it because they must
must.text: A compliance purchase, with no relationship before or after the sale.

unaware.title: Few know what they're covered for
unaware.text: Most people find out the difference at the worst possible moment.

carry.title: You have to carry it, or pay
carry.text: If you can't produce it when you're stopped, you're fined.

same.title: Every product looks the same
same.text: Same cover and the same regulated price, right across the market.

claim.title: Claiming means a call and some hope
claim.text: Support runs through hotlines, and nobody can see where a claim stands.

constraint.title: One hard constraint
constraint.text: No premium discounts, cashback or disguised price incentives. The point is a better experience, not a bought outcome. Everything else is open.

client.title: This is not a hypothetical enterprise partner
client.lead: Tasco is one of Vietnam's major multi-sector groups, listed on the Hanoi Stock Exchange. If you've driven through a toll gate in Vietnam, you've already used something they built.
client.group: The group operates across the entire life of a vehicle and its owner: automotive distribution and retail, electronic toll collection through VETC, insurance, roadside assistance, after-sales service, vehicle care and charging infrastructure. Its nationwide network of showrooms and service centres carries Geely and Lynk & Co, with Mitsui as a strategic shareholder in Tasco Auto.
client.ecosystem: Insurance sits inside that ecosystem rather than beside it. That's why Tasco can see the customer's whole journey — the car, the road, the service centre, the claim — instead of just the policy.

why.title: Why Tasco is doing this at all
why.ambition: Tasco's ambition is to change what insurance feels like for people in Vietnam: protection that's simple to buy, impossible to lose, clear to understand, and straightforward to claim. Millions of drivers currently hold a product they're required to have and nobody has made worth wanting.
why.building: That's the thing you'd be building. Not a feature — the experience itself.

who.title: Who can apply
who.lead: Judged on the solution, not the company. One person with a prototype and a software house with a product in market apply the same way.

win.title: No cash prize. A buyer instead.
win.lead: Most pilots die for one reason: the people in the room couldn't buy anything. This challenge fixes that part first.

yes.title: The people reviewing your work can say yes
yes.text: Tasco's leadership and the business owners who run its insurance operation set the brief, sit at demo day and choose what moves forward. The budget is allocated.

partner.title: A partner that has already done this
partner.text: In September 2026, Tasco led an investment round into BonBon, a startup it first met through its own innovation programme, with GenAI Fund investing alongside.

investment.title: Investment of up to US$100,000
investment.text: Teams that come through the pilot can be considered for investment, on top of the commercial relationship. Offered at the partners' discretion, after due diligence.

directions.title: Directions to build from
directions.lead: Eight places the experience breaks, in the order a customer meets them. Take one, combine several, or make a better case for your own.

buying.label: Buying
buying.lead: Getting covered should take minutes, not a call-back

carrying.label: Carrying
carrying.lead: The policy should be there when it's needed

claiming.label: Claiming
claiming.lead: The worst day should be the simplest part

d1.title: Frictionless purchase and renewal
d1.text: Buy, renew and pay without a queue, a call-back, or a form you fill in twice.

d2.title: Understand before you buy
d2.text: Explain cover in plain language, so people know what they're getting.

d3.title: The right cover for the right person
d3.text: Use consented data to fit protection to one driver, not an average one.

d4.title: Proof in your pocket
d4.text: Digital, instantly verifiable, impossible to lose or leave at home.

d5.title: Help that arrives first
d5.text: Renewal reminders and useful prompts that come before the problem does.

d6.title: Answers at the moment of need
d6.text: Support through chat, voice or in-app, without a hotline queue.

d7.title: Guided claims
d7.text: Tell people what's covered, what's needed, and where their claim stands.

d8.title: Faster assessment
d8.text: Close the gap between filing and resolution.

other.title: Something else entirely
other.text: Combine directions, or bring one nobody has thought of.

efficiency.title: Why efficiency matters here
efficiency.cost: Every piece of friction in this journey costs someone money, and that cost ends up inside the price of protection. Make the end-to-end process genuinely more efficient — and richer in first-party data that customers have agreed to share — and something better becomes possible: insurance that costs less, fits the individual more closely, and is actually worth holding.
efficiency.prize: That's the prize. Not a slicker app — a better deal for the person buying it.

timeline.title: Timeline
timeline.lead: Three weeks, six fixed dates. The build period opens the same day as applications.

start.title: Start on day one
start.text: The build period opens on 23 September — the same day applications do. The written brief, FAQ and submission template are published from day one. The 7 October briefing is a mid-point deep dive with Tasco, not the starting gun. Teams that wait for it lose two of their three weeks.

selection.title: How selection works
selection.text: GenAI Fund screens every submission and selects the ten teams who present. Judges and Tasco's team score live on demo day. No submission sits in a queue for a week.

pilot.title: Winning isn't the end of it. Here's the month that follows.
pilot.lead: Most programmes stop at the trophy and leave “next steps to be discussed”. Here's the actual month, so you can plan the resourcing before you apply.

selection.title: Selection and scoping conversation
selection.text: Tasco confirms which teams it wants to take forward. You present your solution and your commercial case to the leadership team and the business owners who'd run it. Mutual NDA signed.
selection.bring: The demo and a one-page commercial proposal
selection.done: Both sides agree to run a pilot

week1.title: Scope lock
week1.text: You and Tasco agree the exact boundary: which use case, which users, which systems, which success metrics. Data access and approvals are requested here, not later.
week1.bring: Your integration and data requirements in writing
week1.done: A one-page scope both sides have signed

week2.title: Build
week2.text: You build against Tasco's real context in a sandboxed environment, with an assigned business owner on call.
week2.done: The core workflow runs end to end on test data

week3.title: Integrate and checkpoint
week3.text: Connect the agreed systems and hold a mid-point review. Anything not working by this checkpoint doesn't go into week 4.
week3.bring: A working demo against the agreed metrics

week4.title: Test and evaluate
week4.text: Tasco's own team runs the solution against the week-one metrics, with real operational users where approvals allow. You see the results — not a verdict behind closed doors.
week4.done: Results are written up against each metric

decision.title: Tasco decides
decision.text: One of three outcomes, in writing: scale into a production pilot and commercial terms, extend on a revised scope, or stop, with the reasons. You keep the results either way.

pilot.format: The point of a 90-day format is that “no” arrives fast enough to be useful.

note.title: Good to know
note.text: Entering a pilot is Tasco's decision, made after demo day. One month is the target for a tightly scoped pilot — a broader scope runs longer, and the scope is agreed jointly in week 1 before anyone commits. Dates flex with the enterprise's calendar.

myths.title: Five things people get wrong about this
myths.lead: You've probably been burned by something that looked like this. Fair. Here's what's actually true.

rnd.truth: You keep your IP. Mutual NDA before any pilot, and the scope is agreed jointly in week 1 — before you commit engineering time.

procurement.truth: There is no RFP here. The people who set the brief and hold the budget are the people reviewing your work — that's the entire format.

insurance.truth: Most strong submissions don't start there. The written brief, the 7 October session and an assigned business owner close that gap. Bring the solution.

weeks.myth: “Three weeks isn't enough to build anything.”
weeks.truth: Build opens 23 September, not 7 October. And nobody's asking for production software — show what works and how it scales.

prize.myth: “No cash prize — so what's the upside?”
prize.truth: A named enterprise customer, a market, and investment of up to US$100,000 on the table for teams that come through the pilot.

motor.q: Do I have to work on compulsory motor insurance?
motor.a: No. The scope is open: any AI solution that makes the insurance experience better for the people using it. We publish the compulsory motor journey as a worked example because it touches nearly every driver in Vietnam — not because it's the boundary.

wontConsider.q: Is there anything Tasco won't consider?
wontConsider.a: One hard constraint: no premium discounts, cashback, or disguised price incentives. The point is a better experience, not a bought outcome. Everything else is open — make the case for it.

startup.q: Do I need to be a startup?
startup.a: No. Solo builders, student teams, startups, ISVs, systems integrators and enterprise teams can all apply. You're judged on the solution, not the company behind it.

inMarket.q: Can I apply with a product that's already in market?
inMarket.a: Yes — and those submissions often do well, because you can show something working on day one. Tell us what already exists and what you'd build or adapt for Tasco.

win.a: Teams Tasco selects go into a one-month pilot with the business owners who'd run the solution, and teams that come through the pilot can be considered for investment of up to US$100,000. The return is a named enterprise customer and a foothold in Vietnam, not a trophy. (Investment is subject to selection, due diligence and final agreement.)

prizeMoney.a: No. If a cash prize is what you're after, this isn't the right programme — and we'd rather you know that today than on 15 October. What's on offer is a customer.

senior.q: Do I actually get in front of anyone senior?
senior.a: Yes. Tasco's leadership team and the business owners who run its insurance operation set this brief and are in the room at demo day. You're not presenting to an innovation team that then has to go and ask someone.

data.q: Will I get real customer data?
data.a: Assume not. Any development resources are subject to approval. State your data, integration and consent assumptions in your submission — that's part of what makes a proposal credible, and the judging criteria reward it explicitly.

before.q: The briefing is on 7 October. What am I meant to do before then?
before.a: Build. The build period opens on 23 September, the same day applications do, and the written brief, FAQ and submission template are published from day one. The briefing is a mid-point deep dive with Tasco's team — not the starting gun. Teams that wait for it lose two of their three weeks.

ip.a: You do. A mutual NDA is signed before any pilot begins. Commercial terms are agreed directly between you and Tasco, before work starts.

vietnam.q: Do I need to be in Vietnam, or speak Vietnamese?
vietnam.a: No. Applications, the briefing and demo day run in English, virtually. If you reach a pilot, you'll need people who can work with Tasco's team on Vietnam time.

pilot.q: What does the pilot involve, and how long is it?
pilot.a: One month: scope lock, build, integrate, test against agreed metrics, then a written decision to scale, extend or stop. The week-by-week plan is on this page. Entering it is Tasco's decision after demo day, and a broader scope runs longer than a month — the scope is agreed jointly before anyone commits.

hearBack.a: Submissions close 15 October at 23:59 ICT. On 16 October every applicant gets an outcome — shortlisted or not. Ten teams present live on 22 October, and pilot scoping starts on 23 October. No one is left waiting to find out by silence.

rail.note: You don't need a finished product to apply. You need a point of view and three weeks.

documents.today: Delivery documents move on paper and spreadsheets before anyone can reconcile them. Import documents arrive in English and must be filed in Vietnamese, layout intact. HS codes are researched by hand, and import tax is checked by re-keying the same figures.
documents.good: Delivery documents extracted and reconciled, translations that keep their layout, support for HS-code decisions and import-tax reconciliation. People handle the exceptions.

marketing.today: Social culture moves faster than a creative brief. Campaign lessons sit in decks and reports nobody reopens. Budgets are estimated from memory and old quotes.

sales.title: Sales analytics & forecasting
sales.today: Sales data lives in different tools, so the same number gets pulled three ways. Forecasting takes time that should go into acting on it.

manufacturing.title: Smart manufacturing & AI automation
manufacturing.today: Ensuring reliable coffee supply while bringing new assets online, upgrading older machines and launching new products creates pressure on cost and execution. Teams must also keep pace with changing food safety, worker safety and regulatory requirements.
manufacturing.good: Connected equipment, sensors, robotics and AI help teams anticipate failures, automate repetitive tasks, improve quality and make better use of existing assets. Faster commissioning, product testing and production scale-up support new growth, while traceable data and timely alerts support safety and compliance.

legal.today: Contracts are reviewed and tracked by hand. Regulations and emerging issues are monitored manually. Employees ask HR the same policy questions every day.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what personal data BeyondPilot collects, why, who it is shared with, and the choices you have. BeyondPilot is an AI adoption platform backed by GenAI Fund that connects enterprises with AI solutions, talent, use cases, events and programs.

sections.heading: Who we are
body: BeyondPilot operates the website and web application at beyondpilot.ai. For any privacy question or request, write to team@beyondpilot.ai.

sections.heading: What we collect
body: We collect only what the platform needs to work:
items: Account details: your name and email address, and, when you add them, your phone number, country, job title, LinkedIn profile and photo.
Sign-in with Google: your name, email address and profile picture from your Google account. We do not read your Gmail, contacts or files.
What you publish or submit: organization profiles, AI solutions, use cases, proposals, talent profiles and enquiries, and the files you upload with them, such as decks and attachments.
Activity needed to run the service safely: sign-in times, security events and a record of administrative actions.
Technical data: your IP address and browser type in server logs, kept for security and troubleshooting.

sections.heading: How we use it
items: To create and secure your account and sign you in.
To show the profiles, solutions and use cases you choose to publish.
To help enterprises and AI providers find each other, including search and AI-assisted matching of use cases with solutions.
To review applications to programs and challenges, and to send you emails about your account, submissions and decisions.
To keep the platform safe, prevent abuse and meet legal obligations.

sections.heading: AI features
body: Search and matching use AI models to read the text of public profiles, solutions, decks and use cases. That text is sent to our AI provider (OpenAI, directly or through OpenRouter) only to produce search results and match explanations. We do not use your data to train AI models, and our providers process it under their API terms, which do not allow training on it either.

sections.heading: What is public
body: Profiles, solutions and use cases are public only once they are approved and listed. An organization can keep a use case anonymous, and an owner can unlist a solution at any time. Proposals, enquiries, contact details and uploaded files that are not marked public are visible only to you, the people you send them to, and GenAI Fund operators.

sections.heading: Who we share it with
body: We do not sell personal data. We share it only with the service providers that run the platform for us, each bound to use it only for that purpose:
items: Hosting and storage on servers we operate.
Email delivery through Resend.
Sign-in through Google.
AI processing through OpenAI and OpenRouter.
after: We may also disclose data when the law requires it, or to protect the rights and safety of our users.

sections.heading: Cookies
body: We use a session cookie to keep you signed in and a cookie to remember your language. If you accept, Google Analytics sets cookies to measure visits to our public pages; it never runs on pages you sign in to see. We do not use advertising cookies.

sections.heading: How long we keep it
body: We keep your data while your account is active. When you delete your account or ask us to, we delete or anonymize your personal data within 30 days, except what we must keep for legal, security or audit reasons. Submissions to a program may be kept as part of that program's record.

sections.heading: Your choices and rights
body: You can view and edit most of your data in your account. You can also ask us to give you a copy of your data, correct it, delete it, or stop processing it, by writing to team@beyondpilot.ai. We answer within 30 days.

sections.heading: Security
body: We protect data in transit with HTTPS, encrypt stored credentials and provider keys, limit access to operators who need it, and record administrative actions. No system is perfectly secure; if a breach affects you, we will tell you.

sections.heading: International processing
body: Our providers may process data outside your country. When they do, we rely on their contractual safeguards to protect it.

sections.heading: Children
body: BeyondPilot is meant for professionals and is not directed at children under 16. We do not knowingly collect their data.

sections.heading: Changes
body: We will update this page when our practices change, and tell signed-in users about significant changes before they take effect.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: These terms govern your use of BeyondPilot at beyondpilot.ai. By creating an account or using the platform, you agree to them.

sections.heading: The service
body: BeyondPilot helps enterprises and AI providers find each other. It lists AI solutions, talent, use cases, events and programs, and lets you publish your own and apply to programs and challenges. Some features are labelled as previews and may change.

sections.heading: Your account
items: You must give accurate information and keep your sign-in secure.
You are responsible for what happens in your account, and for the organization you act for.
You must be at least 16 and able to enter into this agreement.

sections.heading: What you publish
body: You keep ownership of the content you publish or submit. You allow us to host, display and process it to run the platform, including showing listed content publicly and using it for search and matching. You confirm that you have the right to share it and that it is accurate and lawful.

sections.heading: Review and listing
body: GenAI Fund reviews organizations, solutions, use cases and talent profiles before they are listed, and may decline, unlist or remove content that is inaccurate, misleading or breaks these terms. Approval does not mean endorsement.

sections.heading: Applications and proposals
body: When you apply to a program or send a proposal, its organizers and reviewers can read it. Program outcomes are decided by their organizers. Commercial terms, NDAs and any pilot are agreed directly between the parties; BeyondPilot is not a party to them.

sections.heading: AI features
body: AI-assisted search and matching help you find options faster. Their results may be incomplete or wrong. Check the sources shown and make your own decisions.

sections.heading: Acceptable use
body: Do not:
items: publish false information or impersonate anyone;
send spam or unsolicited commercial messages through the platform;
scrape, copy or resell the directory, or access it by automated means outside the tools we provide;
try to break, overload or bypass the platform's security;
upload unlawful content or content you have no right to share.

sections.heading: Our platform
body: BeyondPilot, its software and design belong to us and our licensors. These terms do not give you any right to them beyond using the platform as offered.

sections.heading: Suspension and closing your account
body: You can stop using BeyondPilot and ask us to close your account at any time. We may suspend or close an account that breaks these terms or puts other users at risk, and will tell you why unless the law prevents it.

sections.heading: Disclaimers and liability
body: The platform is provided as is. We do not guarantee that a listing is accurate, that a match will lead to business, or that the service will always be available. To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for indirect or consequential losses, and our total liability is limited to the amount you paid us in the past 12 months.
